title: When the Autopsy Breaks
premise: Casper Amberdale, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has quietly exposed three staged 'accidents,' is hired by a nervous widow to prove her husband's death hasn't happened yet — a prepayment for a murder that will occur in thirty days. As Casper digs into the victim's shipping company, he discovers a coded ledger hidden in routine invoices that maps a bribery network reaching into the police and the coroner's office. Racing the statute of limitations on the underlying fraud, Casper must choose between protecting the widow — who is both client and suspect — and exposing the powerful men who will kill to keep the ledger buried. In the end, Casper decodes the final entry, confronts the coroner who orchestrated it all, and chooses testimony over self-preservation, trading his anonymity for belonging.
about_author: Paloma Underhill spent a decade as a claims adjuster before turning to fiction, drawing on the quiet dramas hidden inside paperwork. She writes from a coastal town where fog, ledgers, and long memories are local industries.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A frail widow, Edith Vane, retains Casper to prove her husband Gerald's death hasn't happened — payment dated before any body exists. Casper's memory flags her phrasing as rehearsed. The emotional beat: unease; the hook of an impossible retainer pulls him past professional caution into personal obsession.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Dead Yet
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper finds Gerald Vane alive but terrified, working late at Meridian Shipping and refusing to explain. That night Gerald survives a brake failure Casper recognizes as identical to his third solved 'accident.' Beat: dread hardens into certainty — someone is running a pattern, and Casper knows its signature.

chapters.title: Invoices Don't Lie
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Auditing Meridian's books, Casper notices recurring invoice anomalies — round sums, mirrored dates — too regular for error. He photographs every page, building a mental archive. Beat: the thrill of the hunt returns, shadowed by the realization that whoever built this code assumed no one would ever look twice.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper and Detective Ilsa Reyes. Reyes, who once dismissed Casper's earlier findings, reopens one of his old cases and finds the autopsy report suspiciously pristine. Beat: grudging alliance forms; two lonely professionals recognize each other's competence, and something warmer begins to flicker against duty's grain.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper maps the ledger's cipher to a calendar: each entry schedules a death, and Gerald's is thirty days out — the same day the fraud statute expires and evidence becomes worthless. Beat: ticking-clock pressure; Casper realizes solving the murder early destroys nothing unless he can also crack the code in time.

chapters.title: What Edith Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Confronting Edith, Casper learns she isn't a grieving wife but Gerald's sister, and the prepayment was her desperate way of forcing someone competent to intervene before the family name is destroyed. Beat: betrayal curdling into compassion; Casper's suspicion of his own client collapses into protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Long Arm of Meridian
chapters.summary: POV: Reyes. Reyes is ordered off the case by superiors tied to Meridian's board; her files vanish overnight. Casper's apartment is searched with surgical precision — nothing stolen, everything photographed. Beat: fear and isolation; power shows its face, and the two investigators realize they are now the loose ends.

chapters.title: A Death on Schedule
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The ledger's next entry comes due: not Gerald, but the shipping clerk who helped Casper decode the first layer, found drowned exactly as predicted. Beat: grief and guilt; the abstract puzzle acquires a body, and Casper understands the cost of moving too slowly.

chapters.title: The Final Entry
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Under deadline pressure, Casper's memory finally cracks the cipher — the key is the coroner Dr. Ambrose Hale's own signature authentication stamps, meaning Hale authored the schedule himself. Beat: cold clarity at the climax's edge; Casper walks into the morgue knowing Hale must silence him before the statute expires at midnight.

chapters.title: Signed in Presence
chapters.summary: POV: Casper and Reyes. In the morgue's records room, Hale offers Casper partnership and erasure; Casper refuses, reciting the ledger verbatim as Reyes records every word — testimony entered before midnight. Hale falls; the network unravels. Beat: resolution and belonging; Casper trades invisibility for a partner, a purpose, and a name spoken with respect.
